author: Philip Trammell & Anton Korinek
title: Economic Growth under Transformative AI
central_scenario_summary: A review synthesizing growth-theoretic models of transformative AI (TAI), defined as AI that makes capital a close enough substitute for labor to drive growth on its own. The robust finding: fully automating production lets machines self-replicate, dramatically accelerating growth while driving the labor share toward zero, breaking the Kaldor Facts; automating R&D (self-improvement) can amplify this up to hyperbolic 'singularity' growth but may not produce explosion alone. Wages - exploding output times a collapsing labor share - may rise or fall depending on returns to scale, natural-resource constraints, and the direction of technical change; the authors treat these trajectories as plausible within decades or even years and urge institutional preparation.

quotes.text: Recent advances in AI may herald the near arrival of systems that can automate essentially all work.
As AI R&D is automated ever more fully, AI capabilities could advance ever more rapidly.

capability_pace.notes: Central subject is full automation including self-improving AI and singularity-type feedback (hyperbolic growth scenarios). The authors explicitly decline to assign probabilities, but treat these as 'plausible trajectories that could materialize within decades or even years'. Scored 4 for the scenario space reviewed; a conservative reading of their modal case is 3.

expertise_erosion.notes: Labor is homogeneous in the reviewed models; entry barriers, skill premia, and occupational heterogeneity are not discussed.

quotes.text: fully automating production alone (so that machines can self-replicate) would dramatically raise the growth rate and lower the labor share, breaking the Kaldor Facts
Once production is sufficiently automated, output growth is likely to accelerate, and this acceleration will likely continue for the foreseeable future.

productivity_breadth.notes: Economy-wide transformative gains - growth accelerations up to double-exponential or hyperbolic - conditional on TAI arriving.

quotes.text: the central question is whether and when AI will allow capital to become a close enough substitute for labor to drive growth on its own
the burst in output made feasible by a qualitative advance in automation will almost all accrue to capital, driving the labor share toward zero

substitution.notes: TAI is defined by capital becoming a gross substitute for labor. They note capital and labor remain gross complements to date (Nordhaus 2021), so the score reflects the central TAI scenario, not current AI.

demand_absorption.notes: Supply-side growth review; consumer demand elasticities, Baumol saturation, and new-jobs absorption are not analyzed (wages 'depend on... tastes' is the closest touch).

mobility_adjustment.notes: Worker reallocation across occupations is not modeled.

quotes.text: AI may render the claim true in the future, and vindicate Piketty (2014)'s concern about twenty-first century capital concentration.
It may be valuable to consider policy responses that could mitigate extreme distributional consequences

rent_concentration.notes: Concentration is at the factor level: labor share toward zero, output accruing almost entirely to capital owners; the conclusion frames this as 'radical inequality' and 'distributional upheaval' requiring policy. Firm-level market power is not analyzed.

quotes.text: the median forecast on the prediction platform Metaculus places AGI in 2039
plausible trajectories that could materialize within decades or even years

timeline_years.notes: The authors offer no probability assessments of their own; 15 years approximates the Metaculus 2039 AGI median they cite (from the 2026 revision) within their 'decades or even years' framing.

quotes.text: Wages—the product of exploding output and a plummeting labor share—may rise or fall, depending on the returns to scale, the importance of natural resources, and the direction of technical change.

inequality_prediction.notes: Text dimension. Bottom line: under transformative AI the labor share falls toward zero and income concentrates in capital, vindicating Piketty-style concerns about capital concentration; whether absolute wages rise or collapse is genuinely ambiguous, and managing 'radical inequality' becomes a first-order policy problem.
